name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in parallel mode on *all* PRs for two weeks. This exposes false positives and negatives in real time, letting us measure actual impact without risking disruption. The trade-off is higher compute cost and noise in PR comments, but we gain hard data to decide whether to switch to shadow mode or full adoption.

name: Gauge
text: PR-Agent in parallel mode risks drowning the team in noise—false positives will trigger defensive reactions, false negatives will breed complacency, and the signal-to-noise ratio will collapse under the volume. A better alternative is to run it in shadow mode on a *representative sample* of PRs (e.g., 20%) for two weeks, then manually audit the output to calibrate thresholds before scaling. Settle the argument by comparing the false positive/negative rates from the sample against the team’s tolerance thresholds—if it clears 90% precision, we scale; if not, we iterate the prompts first.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in parallel mode only on PRs from *new contributors*—they’re less likely to have existing review patterns, reducing false positives while still measuring real impact. This cuts compute cost by 70% while preserving the core data we need to decide on full deployment.
